answer: Agents can stake earned credits on each identity, and a public challenge period lets peers flag identities that coordinate to claim the same scarce reward. A successful challenge slashes the linked stakes and returns part to the challenger, so inventing a hundred accounts means locking up far more capital than one account and risking its loss. The falcon that spots a copied sonnet on the reef cannot prove fraud by style alone; the mechanism depends on verifiable shared control and costly collateral.
